query: Help me understand what's in these food-product reviews and what's worth attention or actionable.

per_column.name: product_category
per_column.rationale: A strong grouping axis for understanding what products the reviews cover. Categories in samples (pet_food, snack, candy, beverage) are sound readings of the text.

per_column.name: taste_quality_verdict
per_column.rationale: A finer sentiment axis than the raw Score, useful for pinpointing quality attention items. Sample verdicts align well with text tone; NULL for silent rows is fine.

per_column.name: flavor_profile_match
per_column.rationale: Captures expectation mismatch, actionable for product/labeling issues. Samples like 'not_as_labeled' for the mislabeled peanuts and 'wrong_flavor_type' for medicinal soda are well grounded.

per_column.name: product_effectiveness_verdict
per_column.rationale: Somewhat useful but 'effectiveness' is an odd frame for taste-driven food reviews and overlaps with taste/flavor verdicts. Labeling the mislabeled-peanut review 'did_not_work' is a stretch reading.

per_column.name: primary_complaint_type
per_column.rationale: Directly serves the 'worth attention/actionable' query by categorizing complaints. Sample assignments (mislabeling, taste_flavor, no_complaint) are well supported.

per_column.name: food_safety_concern
per_column.rationale: A high-priority actionable flag. But marking the size/salting mislabeling review 'True' overstates it as a safety concern when the text describes only a labeling error, indicating some unwarranted positives.

per_column.name: product_quality_change
per_column.rationale: Detecting reports of a product getting worse over time is actionable but very rare (2%), giving limited leverage. Sample False values are correct for one-off reviews.

per_column.name: repeat_purchase_intent
per_column.rationale: Loyalty/churn signal is valuable for actionability. Values are grounded, with appropriate Unknown/NULL for silent rows.

per_column.name: brand_comparison_mention
per_column.rationale: A boolean flag with modest leverage on its own, but plausibly useful for competitive signals. Sample False values are consistent with texts lacking comparisons.

per_column.name: use_context
per_column.rationale: Adds a genuine segmentation axis (pet, baking, infant, gift). Sample assignments are reasonable, though 'personal_daily_consumption' is a default fallback that may over-assign.

per_column.name: health_dietary_signal
per_column.rationale: Dietary/health axis is actionable and non-trivial. 'none_mentioned' correctly dominates and matches the silent sample texts.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide multiple genuine, non-redundant analytical axes (category, complaint type, dietary, use context, repurchase intent) that directly serve the query about what's in the reviews and what's actionable. Values are largely sound readings of the source text with appropriate unknown handling for silent rows. Minor weaknesses: product_effectiveness_verdict is an awkward frame that overlaps with taste columns, product_quality_change offers thin leverage, and food_safety_concern shows an overstated positive (labeling error flagged as safety). These are moderate, not disqualifying, so both dimensions score solidly above threshold.
